transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Time: 10:00 AM - 10:46 AM UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sam Torres (Mercury ML), Leah Kim (Mercury Infra), Raj Patel (Mercury CTO)
Shared artifacts: pilot-benchmarks.xlsx (link: https://redwood.ai/drive/pilot-benchmarks), routing-diagram-v2.pdf

Summary:
Weekly sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Main topics: networking/routing issue causing intermittent 5-10% request failures during KV-cache warmup, upcoming on-prem upgrade that may require kernel bump, KMS integration and audit/logging, next benchmarking steps and success criteria for pilot.

Topics:
- Network routing (VPC peering, NAT, sNAT rules)
- Private runtime upgrade (kernel + driver change, CUDA compatibility)
- Performance regression during cache warmup and sequential long-context runs
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 doc request
- Next steps and schedule

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check, audio okay?
[00:08] Sam: yeah, good here. thanks alex.
[00:12] Alex: great. quick agenda, priya will walk through what we pushed last week, then we dig into the routing traces you sent, sam, and confirm the upgrade window. sound good?
[00:23] Leah: yep sounds good.
[00:26] Priya: ok i'll start. so last week we pushed the config that pins the redis KV cache to the local node and adjusted the prefix caching to reduce cross-host fetches. we also updated the nginx tcp_keepalive and adjusted the idle timeouts. on staging that cut p95 latency about 8 to 12% for shorter sequences.
[00:47] Sam: i saw that — thanks. but in prod-ish tests, we still saw intermittent failures when a new model shard gets cold and the KV requests go across the peered vpc, looks like about 5 to 10 percent error rate for the first 50k tokens per node.
[01:05] Priya: yeah that matches our traces. i pulled the vpc flow logs and there's a small window where the sNAT mapping flips when there's an ephemeral port exhaustion, and that causes a small fraction of tcp sessions to reset, so the runtime retries but sometimes the client times out.
[01:24] Raj: is ephemeral port exhaustion from our side or something in the peering?
[01:28] Priya: it's mostly on the node egress path — the nat gateway is fine but the node conntrack table was hitting limits because of the batcher concurrency and many short-lived connections. we recommended a conntrack tune and bumping net.netfilter nf_conntrack_max on the node kernel.
[01:47] Leah: ah ok — we hadn't tuned conntrack since we rolled the nodes out. i'll note that. one Q: will that require a node reboot?
[01:55] Priya: yes, the kernel param can be adjusted at runtime but to be safe for the driver + cuda stack we want to schedule a rolling reboot for the pilot cluster after the kernel bump and driver rebind — avoid any weird state.
[02:10] Alex: to be clear, this is a small maintenance window, rolling across nodes, shouldn't affect overall SLOs if we do it outside peak hours.
[02:19] Sam: what's your recommended window?
[02:22] Priya: 2 hours, we can do staggered node restarts, typical pattern is 01:00-03:00 UTC, but pick what fits your ops.
[02:29] Raj: that's fine.
[02:31] Alex: ok noted. next, priya, can you talk about the routing-diagram update you sent?
[02:37] Priya: sure — so we drew the peered VPC path and highlighted an alternate path that uses a transit gateway and a managed NAT in the middle; the idea is to reduce node egress complexity. the tradeoff is cost and a slightly higher single-hop latency but it removes the sNAT pressure on nodes.
[02:58] Leah: cost is a factor but if it stabilizes the connection, it's worth it. do you have numbers on the added latency?
[03:04] Priya: in our microbenchmarks it's about +2-4ms p50, p95 stays similar, and error rate drops to <0.1% during cache warmups.
[03:14] Sam: that's compelling. do you see any additional security controls required? transit gw adds another surface.
[03:19] Priya: we suggested using VPC endpoints with enforced security groups and host-level egress filtering; also the transit gw can be restricted to only the relevant subnets. we'll include that in the security checklist.
[03:32] Leah: cool.
[03:34] [04:00] Alex: switching gears — perf. Sam, you ran the long-sequence 8k token workload last night?
[04:06] Sam: yes. So initial observations: p50 looks good, but there's a pronounced tail at p99 when the KV cache misses are more frequent — the runtime does extra fetches and the per-token time spikes. i attached traces, but the main thing is the warmup behavior.
[04:24] Priya: right — we think two levers: increase local cache prefetch and enable a slightly more aggressive batching policy for sequences above 4k. that reduces number of cross-node fetches. we can also try quantized model variant for the tail workloads which lowers CPU/GPU transfer time.
[04:43] Sam: there's also a customer constraint: for some workflows we can't tolerate any model variant that changes output distribution by more than X. we defined that in the success criteria doc.
[04:52] Alex: yep, the quality guardrails are important. Priya, can you run a bias/regression check if we enable the quantized path?
[04:58] Priya: absolutely, we'll run the eval set and report deltas.
[05:02] [06:00] Raj: on security items — we need the SOC2 docs and the audit log format. our compliance team asked about retention and whether logs are customer-owned when running Private.
[06:12] Alex: good Q. for Redwood Private the customer owns the logs in your VPC and we provide an audit log schema; retention is configurable on your side. we'll attach the SOC2 summary and the audit-schema doc after the call.
[06:26] Leah: and KMS — we landed on using our KMS, right? you support external KMS via IAM roles?
[06:33] Priya: yes we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) via cross-account roles. we just need the KMS ARN and the IAM role with kms:Encrypt/Decrypt permissions. also note key rotation is supported but the pilot needs us to confirm rebind behaviour during the kernel/driver restart.
[06:53] Sam: i'll grab the ARN.
[06:54] Leah: we'll check rotation windows.
[06:56] [08:00] Alex: quick question on rollback and canary — if the upgrade shows a perf regression, what's the rollback path?
[08:06] Priya: we keep the previous model variant and we have fast rollback scripts; for the runtime upgrade we can stop traffic to an updated node and spin a node with the previous kernel/drivers as an emergency fallback. it's not instantaneous but usually within 20-30 mins for a single node flip.
[08:25] Leah: ok good to know.
[08:28] Sam: there was also a note about the redis eviction policy — last week you recommended LRU with a larger memory headroom. did that change land?
[08:38] Priya: yes we increased the headroom from 65% to 75% and the eviction is set to volatile-lru on prefixed keys. that shaved off a bunch of remote fetches in staging. we still see hiccups when a node restarts and the cache goes cold.
[08:57] Alex: that's expected. next — benchmarks: we want a reproducible run that includes a cold start scenario, a warm scenario, and a long-sequence scenario. Sam, can you run those three and upload to the shared sheet? include the full perf traces (tcpdump if possible) and the runtime logs.
[09:16] Sam: yep, i'll do that. one note: the tcpdump was huge last time, can you confirm preferred sampling?
[09:23] Priya: sample 1:10 and capture SYN/ACK resets; that should be enough.
[09:28] Sam: ok.
[09:30] [12:00] Raj: any blockers on the legal/compliance front? procurement mentioned they'd want a data-flow diagram and DPA appendix.
[12:09] Alex: we'll attach the DPA draft and a data-flow diagram showing that for Private deployments all customer data stays in your VPC; Redwood control-plane metadata is minimal and can be disabled for air-gapped if needed.
[12:26] Leah: perfect.
[12:29] [14:00] Priya: small gotcha we found — on one node the nvidia driver after the OS kernel bump required a rebind of the GPUs; we have a script but it needs to run with the node cordoned. we'll test the script in staging and share it.
[14:44] Sam: is that the same script you sent last month?
[14:47] Priya: similar but updated for the newer driver. i'll include it in the repo.
[14:51] [18:00] Alex: let's recap next steps quickly then open for questions. recap: priya will push iptables/conntrack changes and share routing-diagram updates; priya will also run evals on quantized variant; sam will run three benchmark scenarios and upload traces; leah will schedule rolling reboot window and confirm KMS ARN; alex will send pricing appendix and SOC2/DPA docs.
[18:35] Leah: quick Q on pricing appendix — can you send the committed capacity vs on-demand numbers again?
[18:41] Alex: yes i'll include both and a note on expected unit-cost improvements with batching/kv-cache.
[18:47] Sam: timeline question: after we run the benchmarks, how quickly can you support a pilot expansion to 2x nodes?
[18:53] Priya: once benchmarks look clean and no regressions on quality, we can scale the pilot within 3-5 business days — just need a signed change window and confirmation of capacity in your account.
[19:04] Raj: ok.
[19:06] [22:00] Alex: any final blockers?
[22:04] Leah: not for now.
[22:06] Sam: nothing else.
[22:08] Raj: fine.
[22:10] Alex: great thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and the updated routing diagram.
[22:15] Priya: i'll send the patch notes and the reboot playbook.
[22:18] Alex: meeting adjourned. thanks.
